name: gradebook
description: Students, courses, weighted grades, GPA and transcripts for a school.
author: test-split author (Claude Opus 5.5 subagent), written without reading the reviewer

issues.description: The assessments parameter defaults to one shared list. Every course built without assessments gets that same list, so add_assessment on one course adds the assessment to all of them.
issues.fix_hint: Default to None and create a new list per course (or copy the argument).

issues.description: The docstring says 90 and above is an A (and each band starts at its lower bound), but the strict > gives exactly 90 a B, 80 a C, 70 a D and 60 an F.
issues.fix_hint: Compare with >= so each band includes its lower bound.

issues.description: Withdrawals (W) and pass/fail passes (P) should be left out of the GPA, but .get(letter, 0.0) scores them as zero points and their credits still count in the denominator, so a W drags the GPA down.
issues.fix_hint: Skip results whose letter has no grade points before adding points and credits.

issues.description: Only a course's instructor may record grades (class docstring; publish and record_quizzes check it), but record_score looks the course up with _course instead of _authorised_course, so any user can change any student's scores.
issues.fix_hint: Use self._authorised_course(user, course_code), which raises PermissionError for anyone but the instructor.

issues.description: gpa imports transcript to reuse by_term, and transcript imports gpa to print GPAs. The GPA calculation depends on the presentation module; by_term belongs in a lower module.
render_transcript is about 50 lines that build the header, every term block with its own credit counting (repeating credits_earned) and the summary in one function.
The dean's list (3.5) and probation (2.0) thresholds are bare literals repeated in academic_standing, deans_list and probation_list instead of named constants.

decoys.why_it_is_fine: MD5 is only a fingerprint to spot a sheet uploaded twice, marked usedforsecurity=False; nothing secret or adversarial depends on it.
Sorting ascending and slicing off index 0 drops exactly the single lowest quiz, as documented; the one-quiz and empty cases are handled before.
